item.title: China brings childcare closer to families
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- As demand for formal childcare continues to grow among Chinese families, young parents are looking for more affordable, convenient and trustworthy services. China's National Health Commission (NHC) has said efforts are under way to make childcare more accessible, affordable and quality-assured. The country's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) calls for faster development of affordable childcare, including more publicly provided places and a wider range of services. For many families, the first hurdle is price. In 2023, childcare cost an average of 1,978 yuan (about 293 U.S. dollars) per child a month nationwide, excluding meals. In first-tier cities, monthly fees topped 5,500 yuan, pricing out many families. In Baiyin, northwest China's Gansu Province, the city's First People's Hospital runs a childcare center where full-day care costs 750 yuan a month, including three meals and two snacks a day. Baiyin received 100 million yuan in central government funding in 2024 to support affordable childcare. First-time users can also apply for vouchers allowing their children to try a nearby center free for two weeks. Similar efforts to lower costs are under way elsewhere. Nine provinces have introduced childcare subsidies since 2021, while 1,315 county-level regions have offered support ranging from construction and operating subsidies to family vouchers. Over the same period, average fees for full-day childcare fell 29 percent nationwide. Broader family support is also expanding. Since 2025, families have been eligible for 3,600 yuan a year for each child until the age of three. Parents can also deduct 2,000 yuan per child each month from taxable income for children under the age of 3. Location matters too, especially for families with very young children. Ma Liejian, vice president and member of the Secretariat of the All-China Women's Federation, has called for qualified kindergartens to extend services to younger children and for communities to offer full-day, half-day, hourly and temporary childcare close to home. In Beijing, 562 public kindergartens have added nursery classes this year, creating more than 10,000 new places for children aged 2 to 3 and giving more families access to childcare closer to home. Baiyin is following a similar approach. As of April 2025, the city's Baiyin District had 15 registered childcare providers, 13 of them nursery classes in kindergartens, offering a total of 1,360 places. Changsha, capital of central China's Hunan Province, is building a "15-minute childcare service circle" using community space, kindergarten classrooms and workplace facilities. Proximity alone, however, does not solve the problem for parents whose working hours fall outside a conventional childcare day. Yang Fan, vice dean of Renmin University of China's School of Population and Health, said more flexible services, including hourly and holiday care, could better meet the needs of parents in flexible employment or shift work. At a technology park in Shanghai's Yangpu District, an on-site childcare center offers full-day, half-day and hourly care. One project manager said he once booked temporary care through an app just two hours before an unexpected client meeting. In rural Pingdu in east China's Shandong Province, a childcare center converted from unused village property near agricultural greenhouses operates around the clock, giving farming families an option outside conventional daytime hours. For parents of very young children, trust can matter just as much as price or convenience. The same hospital-run center in Baiyin accepts babies as young as three months. Opened in 2021 with 100 places, it has more than 20 certified caregivers. It keeps health records for children and draws on hospital resources for visits by medical experts and multidisciplinary services. Safety is also receiving greater attention at the national level. A draft law on childcare services, submitted to China's national legislature for a first reading in December 2025, includes provisions governing the licensing of childcare providers, staffing, monitoring and emergency response. Zhang Li, deputy dean of the Law School at the China University of Political Science and Law, said the proposed licensing system would allow regulators to screen providers before they begin operating. Requirements for public information disclosure, she said, could also improve transparency, help parents better understand the services on offer and strengthen their confidence in sending children to childcare centers. The draft law's proposal to gradually incorporate inclusive childcare services into the scope of basic public services would strengthen the public-service role of childcare and the government's responsibility for its provision, providing legal support for more stable long-term development, according to He Dan, director of the China Population and Development Research Center under the NHC. In Baiyin, Guo Jianna and her husband are both busy with work, and all three of their children have spent time at the childcare center run by Baiyin's First People's Hospital. Shortly before 5 p.m., Xu Xiaoqin, who oversees the center, began getting the children ready for dinner. By the time Guo arrived to pick up her 2-year-old daughter, the girl had eaten and was ready to go home. "With professional caregivers looking after them, my family and I feel reassured," Guo said. ■

item.title: Chinese icebreakers Xuelong, Xuelong 2 return after fruitful Arctic expedition
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
Members of China's 16th Arctic Ocean scientific expedition wave to relatives and friends on the research icebreaker Xuelong 2 at the base dock in Shanghai, east China, Sept. 30, 2026. China's research icebreakers Xuelong and Xuelong 2, or Snow Dragon and Snow Dragon 2, returned to Shanghai in east China on Wednesday after nearly three months of the country's 16th Arctic Ocean expedition. Organized by the Ministry of Natural Resources, the expedition was carried out by four vessels: Xuelong, Xuelong 2, Jidi and Tansuo-3. As of now, Jidi and Tansuo-3 are still on their research missions and are expected to return in mid-October. (Xinhua/Wen Jinghua) SHANGHAI, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- China's research icebreakers Xuelong and Xuelong 2, or Snow Dragon and Snow Dragon 2, returned to Shanghai in east China on Wednesday after nearly three months of the country's 16th Arctic Ocean expedition. The expedition successfully completed key tasks, including comprehensive investigation and monitoring, cutting-edge scientific research, and international cooperation. According to the expedition team, both the scale of the expedition and the total number of tasks reached new highs. It achieved fruitful results in new scientific discoveries, theoretical breakthroughs, technological tests, and equipment applications, providing strong support for a deeper understanding of and effective response to global climate change and promoting sustainable development in the Arctic. Organized by the Ministry of Natural Resources, the expedition was carried out by four vessels: Xuelong, Xuelong 2, Jidi and Tansuo-3. item.title: Firm opposition to "Taiwan independence" serves common interests of China, U.S.: mainland spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- Firmly opposing separatist activities seeking "Taiwan independence" and maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait serve the common interests of both China and the United States, a Chinese mainland spokesperson said on Wednesday. Zhang Han, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks at a regular press conference in response to a question about recent discussion over the role of the Taiwan question in China-U.S. relations. Reiterating that the Taiwan question is at the very core of China's core interests and the bedrock of the political foundation of China-U.S. relations, Zhang said that proper handling of the Taiwan question would help maintain overall stability in China-U.S. relations, while mishandling it could lead to confrontation or even conflict and push bilateral ties into a highly dangerous situation. Zhang said Taiwan authorities led by Lai Ching-te have persisted in their separatist position and refused to recognize the 1992 Consensus, which embodies the one-China principle, while repeatedly making moves in pursuit of "Taiwan independence." "It is the main source of disruption to peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait," Zhang said, calling on people on both sides of the Strait to work together to advance national reunification. The Taiwan question stems from a full-blown civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the remnants of the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, and the CPC founded the People's Republic of China (PRC). The unresolved civil war and foreign interference have left the two sides of the Taiwan Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation, though the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. In a separate response to a question about remarks by a Taiwan politician, who accused the mainland of deliberately misinterpreting UN General Assembly Resolution 2758 to prevent Taiwan from participating in international organizations, Zhang rejected the claims as a distortion of facts. She said Resolution 2758 made clear that restoring the lawful rights of the PRC is essential both for the protection of the UN Charter and for the cause that the UN must serve under the Charter. Zhang added that the Taiwan authorities' repeated attempts to distort and attack Resolution 2758 and challenge the authority of the UN and the postwar international order were bound to fail. The UN General Assembly adopted Resolution 2758 in 1971 by an overwhelming majority, clarifying that the PRC government is the sole legal government representing the whole of China. This resolution, from the perspective of international law, completely eliminated possibilities of "two Chinas" or "Taiwan independence." ■

item.title: China's manufacturing PMI at 50.1 in September
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- The purchasing managers' index (PMI) for China's manufacturing sector stood at 50.1 in September 2026, up 0.3 percentage points from August and back to the expansion zone, official data showed on Wednesday. A reading above 50 indicates expansion, while a reading below 50 signifies contraction. The manufacturing sector's business climate improved further in September, with the PMI rising for a second consecutive month, said Huo Lihui, a chief statistician with the National Bureau of Statistics. Among the 21 industries surveyed, 12 reported a PMI above the expansion threshold, four more than the previous month, Huo noted. The sector saw expansion in both manufacturing output and market demand in September. The production sub-index climbed to 51.7, up 1.3 percentage points from August, while the new orders index was at 50.5, still above the threshold. Driven by the acceleration in production, enterprises' willingness to purchase strengthened, with the procurement volume index reaching 51.0, an increase of 0.5 percentage points from the previous month, said Huo. PMI for the equipment manufacturing industry, the high-tech manufacturing industry and the consumer goods industry stood at 51, 52.5 and 50.7, respectively, all remaining in the expansion zone. Affected by rising international commodity prices and growing demand in some industries, the purchasing price index for major raw materials and the ex-factory price index for manufacturing stood at 60.8 and 54, respectively, up 4.2 percentage points and 3.6 percentage points from the previous month. PMI for medium-sized and small manufacturing enterprises came in at 49.7 and 48.9, respectively, increases of 0.3 percentage points and 1 percentage point from the previous month, as business activity picked up. ■

The article by Xi, also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, will be published in this year's 19th issue of the Qiushi Journal, a flagship magazine of the CPC Central Committee. item.title: Xi, Brunei's Sultan exchange congratulations on 35th anniversary of ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and Sultan of Brunei Haji Hassanal Bolkiah Mu'izzaddin Waddaulah on Wednesday exchanged congratulations on the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries. Xi noted that the traditional friendship between China and Brunei has a long history and remained strong over time. In the process of working together towards modernization, the two countries have set an example of mutual respect, equality and common development between large and small countries, Xi added. Over the 35 years since the establishment of diplomatic ties, China and Brunei have steadily deepened political mutual trust, achieved fruitful results in cooperation across various fields, and strengthened people-to-people exchanges, he said. Xi said that last year, Hassanal paid a state visit to China, during which the two sides reached important consensus on building a China-Brunei community with a shared future, ushering bilateral relations into a new stage of historical development. Xi emphasized that he attaches great importance to the development of China-Brunei relations and is willing to work with Hassanal to take the 35th anniversary of diplomatic ties as an opportunity to carry forward traditional friendship, enhance the alignment of development strategies, deepen mutually beneficial cooperation, and advance the building of the China-Brunei community with a shared future in a more substantive and in-depth manner, so as to better benefit the two peoples and contribute more to regional prosperity and stability. Hassanal stated that over the past 35 years since establishing diplomatic relations, Brunei and China have consistently trusted, respected, and understood each other. In 2025, the two countries reached an important consensus on building a community with a shared future, he added. He looks forward to taking the 35th anniversary of Brunei-China diplomatic relations as an opportunity to further strengthen bilateral ties, deepen cooperation and exchanges in areas such as economy, trade, investment, defense, and culture, and jointly achieve prosperity and progress for both countries, thereby better benefiting their peoples. ■

item.title: Xi pays tribute to national heroes on Martyrs' Day
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
Chinese President Xi Jinping straightens the ribbon on a flower basket during a ceremony to present flower baskets to fallen national heroes at Tian'anmen Square in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 30, 2026. Xi Jinping and other leaders of the Communist Party of China and the state including Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng attended the ceremony on Wednesday. The event was held to mark Martyrs' Day. Observed on Sept. 30, one day before National Day, the day commemorates those who gave their lives for national independence and prosperity. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and other Party and state leaders attended a ceremony to present flower baskets to fallen national heroes at Tian'anmen Square in central Beijing on Wednesday morning. The event was held to mark Martyrs' Day. Observed on Sept. 30, one day before National Day, the day commemorates those who gave their lives for national independence and prosperity. Since Martyrs' Day was established in 2014, Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, has maintained the tradition of paying homage to fallen heroes on the day. The other leaders who attended the ceremony on Wednesday included Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng. They were joined by representatives from all walks of life. At 10 a.m., all attendees sang the national anthem, followed by a moment of silence in tribute to the heroes who sacrificed their lives for the liberation of the Chinese people and the development of the People's Republic of China. Nine large flower baskets were placed in front of the Monument to the People's Heroes. Xi and other leaders walked up to the foot of the monument, where he straightened the ribbons on the baskets. Then, they walked around the monument to pay their tributes. The baskets, with ribbons reading "Eternal Glory to the People's Heroes," were presented in the name of the CPC Central Committee; the National People's Congress Standing Committee; the State Council; the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference; the Central Military Commission; non-Communist parties, the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce, and patriots without party affiliations; people's organizations and people from all walks of life; veterans, retired senior officials and the relatives of martyrs; and Chinese Young Pioneers. Yin Li, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and secretary of the CPC Beijing Municipal Committee, presided over the ceremony. This year marks the 105th founding anniversary of the CPC and the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March, which lasted from 1934 to 1936.
